title: Right-Hand Front Door Speaker Removal and Refitting
introduction:
This guide covers the right-hand front door midwoofer and woofer on Mustangs with the documented MyFord Touch interface. The source heading covers SYNC 2/SYNC 3, but this complete workflow is limited to the supplied MyFord Touch operating instructions; verify that interface before work. The drawings identify each speaker, its mounting bolts and its electrical connection; they do not diagnose a sound complaint.

I treat the door trim like a lid with strings attached: releasing its clips does not free its wiring or latch cable. Work through those attachments in order, and speaker access becomes a controlled unwrapping job instead of a tug-of-war.

requirements.category: Match the documented audio interface before starting

items.name: MyFord Touch interface required for this complete workflow
items.detail: Before dismantling anything, confirm that the fitted system has the documented MyFord Touch Home screen with the lower-left Entertainment corner, AM/FM tabs and the Power, VOL, TUNE and Seek controls described in the completion check. This workflow narrows the source’s SYNC 2/SYNC 3 heading to the interface supported by the supplied owner instructions. If the car has SYNC 3 or a different interface, stop before dismantling and obtain the complete matching owner control sequence and applicable repair instructions; this article does not verify that branch.

items.name: Prevent unexpected starting
items.detail: Park on level ground with the parking brake applied and wheels chocked; keep P selected on an automatic or a parked gear on a manual. Keep the engine stopped throughout. Disable remote start, if equipped, through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before dismantling anything. Otherwise, someone could remotely start the car, causing personal injury or death. If the setting needs ignition power, keep the valid intelligent access key inside. From confirmed OFF, press and release START/STOP without pressing either pedal to select engine-off ON. If already ON for the settings, leave it ON rather than toggling it. After the setting change, return ON to OFF by pressing and releasing the button without pressing a pedal; if already OFF, leave it OFF. With the ignition OFF, remove the key from the vehicle before service to prevent another person from starting the engine; an accidental start may cause serious personal injury. Review [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

items.name: Protect eyes, ears and hands
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection while servicing the vehicle. Wear protective gloves when handling parts with sharp or pointed edges. Failure to follow these precautions may result in serious personal injury. Review the applicable guidance in [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189) before beginning.

items.name: Trim removal and torque tools
items.detail: Have a trim removal tool for lifting the window-switch bezel assembly, as shown in the switch reference, and a torque tool suitable for the specified inch-pound fastener settings.

items.name: Upper trim panel bolt
items.detail: The bolt behind the interior door-release-handle cover is tightened during refitting to 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm).

items.name: Center trim panel bolt
items.detail: The bolt exposed after removing the window-switch bezel assembly is tightened during refitting to 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm).

items.name: Lower trim panel retainers
items.detail: Remove both lower-edge fastener retainers before releasing the panel clips. Their refitting torque is 13 lb.in (1.5 Nm).

items.name: Trim-panel illustration applicability
items.detail: The [Front Door Trim Panel](#/document/G1692600) reference shows LHD and the RH door; RHD and the LH door are similar. This article remains specific to the RH speaker.

items.name: Window-switch assembly
items.detail: Use [Front Door Window Control Switch (501-11 Glass, Frames and Mechanisms, Removal and Installation)](#/document/G1695936) for the nested access operation. Its LHD illustration shows the LH side; RHD and the RH side are similar. For speaker access, remove the switch and bezel together and disconnect the switch connector. Leave the switch attached to its bezel for this job.

edits.text: NOTE: The removal instructions also include details needed for installation.
edits.why: I keep the refitting information in view while taking things apart, particularly the fastener torque notes.

edits.text: Remove the front door trim panel. Refer to: [Front Door Trim Panel (501-05 Interior Trim and Ornamentation, Removal and Installation)](#/document/G1692600).
edits.why:
Start at the interior door-release handle: remove its small cover and the upper trim bolt behind it. At the armrest, use the trim removal tool to lift the window-switch and bezel assembly upward, releasing its four retaining clips, then disconnect the switch electrical connector. Remove the exposed center trim bolt and both lower-edge fastener retainers.

Release the panel progressively, pulling each working area away from the door. At the rear upper edge, release the clip first, then both pin-type retainers. Continue around the rear and lower edge: release the pin-type retainer first, then the clip near the lower speaker grille. At the front edge, near the hinges, release the lower pin-type retainer first, then both upper pin-type retainers. All three front-edge retainers must be free before lifting the panel.

Lift the panel up and out of the door. Disconnect its electrical connectors, if equipped. With access to the back of the interior-handle bracket, disengage the latch-cable retaining fitting diagonally down and to the right in the supporting backside view, moving it out of the bracket, then free the latch cable and remove the panel. That direction describes the backside illustration, not a universal vehicle-forward direction. The cable is the final tether; releasing the perimeter clips alone does not make the panel free.

edits.text: Remove the mounting bolts and move the door midwoofer speaker away from its mounting.
edits.why: The drawing identifies the smaller speaker assembly with three mounting bolts around its flange. Its electrical connector is at the lower-left edge of the illustrated assembly, so the speaker remains connected until the next action.

edits.text: Disconnect the midwoofer speaker electrical connector to free the speaker. Installation bolt torque: 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm).
edits.why: The torque applies to the speaker mounting bolts during refitting. The connector is a separate electrical attachment, not a threaded fastener.

edits.text: Remove the mounting bolts and move the door woofer speaker away from its mounting.
edits.why: The drawing identifies the larger round speaker and its three perimeter mounting bolts. Its electrical connector sits at the lower-left edge in this view; free that connection before taking the speaker away.

edits.text: Disconnect the woofer speaker electrical connector to free the speaker. Installation bolt torque: 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm).
edits.why: Use this torque for the woofer mounting bolts during refitting. Keeping the connector and mounting hardware as separate tasks makes the reverse sequence clear.

edits.text: Install by reversing the removal sequence. Reconnect each removed speaker, position it on its mounting and tighten its bolts to the torque stated beside that speaker. Transfer trim-panel parts as necessary, then refit the trim panel and window-switch assembly in reverse order.
edits.why:
Before hanging the panel, reconnect the latch cable. Viewed from behind the panel in the same orientation used for removal, return its retaining fitting diagonally up and to the left into the handle bracket so it is seated again. Reconnect the panel electrical connectors, if equipped, then bring the panel into position and lower its upper edge into place, reversing the lift-up-and-out removal movement.

Restore the perimeter attachments in reverse order: seat both upper front-edge pin-type retainers, then the lower front-edge pin-type retainer. At the rear and lower edge, engage the clip near the lower speaker grille, then the pin-type retainer. At the rear upper edge, engage both pin-type retainers, then the clip. This restores all three front-edge retainers as well as the rear and lower attachments.

Reinstall the lower fastener retainers and center bolt using the trim torque settings in the preparation section. Reconnect the window-switch connector and press the switch-and-bezel assembly back into the armrest until its retaining clips are seated. Reinstall the upper trim bolt at its specified torque, then its cover. I check that the cable fitting, disconnected plugs and all released trim attachments are restored before calling the refit complete; a tidy-looking panel can still hide an unfinished connection.

After all wiring and trim are restored, keep the car parked in P for an automatic or a parked gear for a manual, with the parking brake applied, wheels chocked and the engine stopped. With the valid key inside, start from ignition OFF and press the start button without pressing either pedal to switch the ignition ON without starting the engine. For the documented MyFord Touch interface, if the audio is OFF, press the audio Power button to turn it ON; if it has already resumed ON, leave it ON rather than toggling it. Touch the Home icon, then the lower-left Entertainment corner and the AM or FM tab. Turn TUNE or press Seek to find a familiar station, then turn VOL to a comfortable level and listen for sound from the serviced door speakers. This is an ordinary function check, not fault isolation. After listening, press the audio Power control to turn the audio OFF. With ignition still in the known engine-off ON state, check the disturbed window switch: keep children and pets away and hands and objects clear of the glass; press the window switch to open the window and lift it to close. Confirm normal response without testing or overriding bounce-back. Press and release START/STOP without pressing either pedal to return the known ON state to OFF. With the ignition OFF, remove the key. Keep the parked gear, parking brake and wheel restraints in place. Gently open and close the door with its handle, confirming the interior handle releases the latch and the door latches normally without forcing it. These are ordinary checks of the disturbed controls and connections, not electrical diagnosis or door alignment. If sound, window response, handle action or retention is abnormal, stop before driving and keep ignition OFF/key out before reopening trim or checking a connector. See the [matching owner manual, Audio, Windows and Starting](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/Catalog/owner_information/2015-Mustang-Owners-Manual-version-1_om_EN-US_07_2014.pdf) for the fitted controls.
